title: Reliability bridgework tactical plan Q4 2026
summary: A short, execution-oriented plan that creates temporary 'bridge' squads to align product feature teams, platform engineering, and SRE around operationalizing SLOs and improving error budgets across three priority services. Emphasis on fast experiments, concrete configuration changes, and an explicit handoff cadence to product owners and platform owners.
objectives: Reduce P95 request latency regression incidents for inference-api by 30% vs baseline within two release cycles
Establish repeatable SLO onboarding checklist that reduces time-to-onboard from feature launch to SLO-backed alerts from 6 weeks to 2 weeks
Create a play-for-fallback policy and A/B fault-injection runbook for two critical routes to test graceful degradation
Demonstrate 15% token-cost reduction for common chat workloads through targeted batching + caching changes without increasing error rate
scope: Focus on three services: inference-api (hosted), routing-service, and kv-cache. Work spans monitoring rules, runbook drafts, alert tuning, small-runtime config changes (batching thresholds, cache TTLs), and two controlled chaos experiments. Not in scope: full model quantization program, Dedicated capacity procurement, or major infra refactors.
approach: Form 3 temporary bridge squads (2 engineers from product team + 1 SRE + 1 platform engineer) per service
Run 4 two-week tactical sprints with clear sprint goals and ship small, reversible changes
Use experiment-driven changes: shadow configs, traffic ramp, and rollback windows documented in each change ticket
Track success through a compact dashboard: SLO burn-rate, P50/P95/P99 latency, error budget consumption, and per-token cost delta
roles_and_responsibilities: Bridge Lead (Aisha Patel) - coordinates cross-squad cadence, removes blockers, owns executive updates
SRE pair - implements alerts, runbooks, and incident postmortems for experiments
Platform engineer - vets config changes for safety and deployability, owns canary automation
Product engineer - owns product acceptance criteria, verifies UX/latency tradeoffs
Analytics partner (Kavya Iyer) - provides daily SLO burn dashboards and helps validate metrics
timeline_milestones: Sprint 0 (7/20-8/2): discovery, baseline measurement, runbook skeletons, and safety gates
Sprint 1 (8/3-8/16): batching and cache experiment rollout in shadow, small alert tuning
Sprint 2 (8/17-8/30): controlled traffic ramp for batching, begin chaos test #1 (partial region failover)
Sprint 3 (8/31-9/13): fallback policy test, finalize onboarding checklist, iterate alerts
Sprint 4 (9/14-9/27): consolidate changes, document handoffs, executive demo and decision on broader rollout
Post-project (9/28-10/12): transition to ops, full runbook publication, backlog of follow-ups to product and platform teams
success_metrics: Primary: 30% reduction in P95 latency regression incidents for inference-api across two releases
Secondary: Average SLO onboarding time reduced to <=2 weeks for new routes using the checklist
Operational: Alert noise down by 40% (fewer duplicate/non-actionable alerts)
Cost: 15% per-token compute cost reduction on measured chat workload cohort
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: experiments cause customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: shadow first, staged traffic ramp, automatic rollback after threshold breaches
Risk: bridge squads block on platform capacity. Mitigation: reserved canary lanes and prioritization with platform-on-call
Risk: insufficient analytics fidelity for burn-rate. Mitigation: dedicate analytics engineer for first two sprints and add metric instrumentation tickets to Sprint 0
Risk: ownership gaps at handoff. Mitigation: mandatory 2-week overlap and signed acceptance checklist from product and platform owners
next_steps: Finalize bridge squad rosters and publish sprint cadence calendar by 2026-07-18
Create Sprint 0 confluence page with baseline dashboards and runbook template (owner: Diego Morales)
Open JIRA epic JIRA-RLY-879 and create child tasks for monitoring gaps, config changes, and chaos experiments
Schedule cross-functional kickoff 2026-07-20 10:00 UTC and reserve 90 minutes
notes: This doc is intentionally tactical and lightweight. Expect iteration after Sprint 0. Keep changes small and reversible; the primary goal is repeatability and a crisp handoff path to steady-state operations. Slack channel #bridgework-sre will be used for daily standups and quick escalations.
